classification.difficultyReason: Infer bounds on both quartiles from the intact cumulative bars, combine those bounds with the IQR to force their values, then use ordered positions to minimise the missing cumulative frequency and check attainability.

content.prompt: A cumulative frequency histogram for a dataset of 50 scores is partially damaged, obscuring the heights of the bars for scores 16 and 17. The remaining bars are intact. It is known that the IQR is 2. What is the minimum height of the bar, $y$?

spec.description: Cumulative histogram with intact bars and hatched damaged columns labelled y and x. The illustrative tops of the damaged regions are not numerical givens. Hatching denotes obscured information.
spec.mathematics: Scores 15–20; intact cumulative frequencies 4, 40, 46 and 50 at scores 15, 18, 19 and 20 respectively. Frequencies at 16 and 17 are unknown.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
There are 50 scores. Each half contains 25 observations, so $Q_1$ is the 13th score and $Q_3$ is the 38th score.
Only four scores are 15, so $Q_1\ge16$. The cumulative frequency at 18 is 40, so $Q_3\le18$.
Since $Q_3-Q_1=2$, these bounds force $Q_1=16$ and $Q_3=18$.
The 13th score must be 16, so at least 13 scores must be at most 16. Hence $y\ge13$.
This is attainable with cumulative frequencies $y=13$ and $x=35$: the 13th score is 16 and the 38th score is 18. Therefore $y_{\min}=13$.
